items.title: docs(id): feature-leveled build variants design record (#5788)
items.body: Design decision record for issue #5788 (queue task 14139, lane code-k). Settles the four-level variant set (L0 embedded/provider, L1 client-only, L2 headless service, L3 full node) with the capability matrix that defines them; variants as composition crates with cargo features confined to seam crates; per-variant budgets under the #3447 perf-first order; conformance via the determinism replay fixtures as cross-variant oracles plus shell/receipt contracts; #1066 upgrade behaviour per variant including the client-only degrade contract; and answers to the issue's three open questions (release artefacts vs build-time, no lite-server level, variant-drift ownership). Verified against origin/main 129df4af83 and the task 13679 triage evidence. Docs-only; no code change. Closes #5788. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Added a design record describing four planned build levels, their capabilities, and linkage boundaries. * Documented performance and artifact expectations, compatibility and upgrade behavior, and checks for consistency across variants. * Outlined the proposed implementation sequence and alternatives considered. These changes document plans; they do not add build variants.

items.title: S1 of #14056: feature catalogue + manifest + hash as design-of-record
items.body: Part of #14056 — slice S1 (design-of-record). Does not close the issue: S2–S13 remain. Implemented by fleet lane oc-code-01 (task 23310), which pushed this branch and parked before opening the PR; taken over, independently verified, and landed by lane ITEM-WORK-107 under the same task claim. ## What this adds `pkgs/id/composition/` — plan §4 + §5 as machine-readable design-of-record: - `catalogue.toml` — the §4 feature catalogue as data: 33 features with declared dependencies, compile/host/consume roles, and 3 exclusivity groups (alternate stores mutually exclusive); 7 profiles (`plain`, `full`, `headless` with `basement` as its alias, `embedded`, `composer-host`, `alt-store-node`, `hosted-edge`); the unrepresentable list. - `manifest-schema.md` — the §5.1 manifest schema (alias-first resolution, closed catalogue, exclusivity refusal, requires closure, open profile sets). - `composition-hash-spec.md` — the §5.2 canonical hashing spec: BLAKE3-256 over canonical CBOR, with a worked example and golden vector. - `examples/` + `golden/` — example manifests and the golden vector (`inputs.json`, `canonical.hex` 464 bytes, `hash.hex`), reproducible via `golden/recheck.sh`. - `validate.py` — executable validation of the catalogue against today's tree. - S1 record note in `doc/2026-11-24T03-36-48Z_design_id-feature-composition/s1-catalogue-manifest-hash.md`. - §0.2 reconciliation appended as an amendment section to the #5788 predecessor record (`doc/2026-11-09T04-43-05Z_design_id5788_build_variants.md`), per that record's own amendment rule — nothing above the amendment rewritten. All five 2026-11-24 amendments are honoured: roles on every feature (descriptive only), `headless` canonical + `basement` alias resolving before hashing, server/client as roles not node classes, strategy behaviours as world conventions, and the `rust` feature as the compile prerequisite (catalogue entry + in `roc-composer`'s requires). ## Verification (independent re-run by the landing lane) - `python3 -I validate.py` → pass, no warnings; all 7 profiles resolve (plain 0, full 23, headless 5, embedded 0, composer-host 8, alt-store-node 24, hosted-edge 5). - `bash golden/recheck.sh` → canonical bytes reproduce (464 bytes); hash reproduces: `960b3f97e0656713540e593d803c752b5ccca6c6cb47f01cb896e121c6557f78`. - Branch is one commit on top of main; all files new except the one doc amendment append. Known findings recorded for later slices (not S1 failures): `id-web/sandbox` forwarding gap → S2; `world` conflation → S3 split; core-default group overlap warning until S6. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
